mangrove-planting-ranong-2015-tokio-mari: Nine photographs from the mangrove planting activity of Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance held in Ranong province, southern Thailand, from 26 to 30 January 2015. The group's mangrove planting project began in 1999 from a suggestion by its own employees, and this visit marked fifteen years of the work in Thailand — the volunteers' shirts read "15th Anniversary Tokio Marine & Nichido Mangrove Project Thailand, 2000-2015". Green Volunteers travelling from the Tokyo head office joined staff of Tokio Marine Insurance (Thailand) on site. The planting ground was at Ban Ngao in Ranong: the board there reads "Thai-Japan Friendship Through Mangrove Planting Project" and "Mangrove Forest : Forest for Life", and records five hectares planted for the 2014 season — the sixty-third planting — in coordination with OISCA (Thailand), the Department of Marine and Coastal Resources, and the Ngao Mangrove Conservation Community. The set holds the group portrait beneath the welcome banner at the Tinidee Hotel in Ranong, the departure from Suvarnabhumi airport, the ceremony staged among an exhibition of photographs, the boat upriver with DMCR rangers, the briefing before the site board, two frames with local schoolchildren, the volunteers on the riverbank, and the sun going down over the sea. tokio-marine-malayan-insurance-manila-19: Three photographs from the party held to mark the change of corporate name of Tokio Marine's Philippine company, Tokio Marine Malayan Insurance Co., Inc. The banner in the hall reads "TOKIO MARINE MALAYAN INSURANCE CO., INC. (Formerly Pan Malayan Insurance Corp.) Honoring the Visit of Mr. Higuchi and Celebrating the Change of Corporate Name" — the evening joined a visit from the Tokyo head office with the retirement of the old name, Pan Malayan Insurance. Tokio Marine had entered the Philippine market in 1964 through a joint venture with the Malayan Group of the Yuchengco family; the president of Tokio Marine in this period was Koukei Higuchi, who held the office from 1996 to 2001. Shinkichi Miki was posted to Manila for five years from the late 1990s, directly after his playing career ended. The set holds the group portrait before the banner, a portrait at a residence, and one taken around the president's desk at the Manila office. These are scans of film prints and no date was recorded with them. The company itself was absorbed into Malayan Insurance in July 2008 and the name has since disappeared.
